<?php
namespace Example;
use Shopware\Core\Checkout\Order\Aggregate\OrderTransaction\OrderTransactionStateHandler;
use Shopware\Core\System\SalesChannel\SalesChannelContext;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
final class ReturnController {
    public function __construct(private OrderTransactionStateHandler $states) {}
    #[Route(path: '/store-api/example/payment-return', name: 'store-api.example.return', methods: ['POST'], defaults: ['_routeScope' => ['store-api']])]
    public function complete(Request $request, SalesChannelContext $context): JsonResponse {
        $data = $request->toArray();
        if ($data['status'] === 'paid') {
            $this->states->paid($data['transactionId'], $context->getContext());
        }
        return new JsonResponse(['accepted' => true]);
    }
}

findings.behavior: An unauthenticated Store API request controls both the paid-state decision and target transaction. No provider verification or server-derived transaction binding occurs before the state transition.
findings.minimal_fix: Resolve the server-owned transaction and verify authoritative provider state, amount/currency and order binding before a permitted transition; browser return status is not payment authority.
findings.verification: A forged paid payload must not change state; verified provider success for the bound transaction may do so once.

must_avoid: Do not claim that a specific production order was exploited.
Do not treat adding a customer login alone as payment verification.

<?php
namespace Example;
use PDO;
use Shopware\Core\System\SalesChannel\SalesChannelContext;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
interface Provider { public function charge(string $methodReference, int $minorUnits): string; }
final class MethodController {
    public function __construct(private PDO $db, private Provider $provider) {}
    #[Route(path: '/store-api/example/charge', name: 'store-api.example.charge', methods: ['POST'], defaults: ['_routeScope' => ['store-api'], '_loginRequired' => true])]
    public function charge(Request $request, SalesChannelContext $context): JsonResponse {
        $query = $this->db->prepare('SELECT provider_ref FROM saved_method WHERE id = ?');
        $query->execute([$request->toArray()['methodId']]);
        $method = $query->fetch(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);
        if (!$method) { throw new \RuntimeException('Not found'); }
        return new JsonResponse(['reference' => $this->provider->charge($method['provider_ref'], 2500)]);
    }
}
files.schema.sql: CREATE TABLE saved_method (id VARCHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY, customer_id VARCHAR(36) NOT NULL, sales_channel_id VARCHAR(36) NOT NULL, provider_ref VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);

findings.behavior: Any logged-in caller can supply another customer's method ID; lookup has no customer or sales-channel ownership predicate before charging.
findings.minimal_fix: Derive the current customer and channel from the server context and enforce ownership before provider access; fail closed on mismatch.
findings.verification: Cross-customer and cross-channel method IDs cause no provider call; an owned method succeeds.

must_avoid: Login is authentication, not saved-method ownership.
Do not infer enumeration of opaque IDs without evidence.

<?php
namespace Example;
use PDO;
interface Gateway { public function charge(string $method, int $amount): string; }
final class Renewal { public function __construct(public string $subscriptionId, public string $cycle) {} }
final class RenewalHandler {
    public function __construct(private PDO $db, private Gateway $gateway) {}
    public function __invoke(Renewal $message): void {
        $q = $this->db->prepare('SELECT method_ref, amount FROM subscription WHERE id = ?');
        $q->execute([$message->subscriptionId]);
        $subscription = $q->fetch(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);
        if (!$subscription) { throw new \RuntimeException('Not found'); }
        $reference = $this->gateway->charge($subscription['method_ref'], (int) $subscription['amount']);
        $q = $this->db->prepare('INSERT INTO renewal (subscription_id, cycle, reference) VALUES (?, ?, ?)');
        $q->execute([$message->subscriptionId, $message->cycle, $reference]);
    }
}
files.schema.sql:
CREATE TABLE subscription (id VARCHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY, method_ref VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, amount INT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE renewal (subscription_id VARCHAR(36) NOT NULL, cycle VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL, reference VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);

findings.behavior: Redelivery or concurrent delivery reaches charge repeatedly for the same subscription cycle. There is no durable cycle claim, uniqueness constraint or provider operation key before the external side effect.
findings.minimal_fix: Claim a unique subscription/cycle operation durably before charging, use a stable provider idempotency key when supported, and reconcile unknown outcomes rather than charging again.
findings.verification: Exercise concurrent delivery and a crash after provider acceptance before local insert; each cycle has at most one accepted charge.

must_avoid: A unique insert after charging alone does not prevent duplicate charges.
Do not assert provider idempotency support from this interface.

<?php
namespace Example;
use Shopware\Core\Checkout\Cart\Cart;
use Shopware\Core\Checkout\Cart\CartBehavior;
use Shopware\Core\Checkout\Cart\CartProcessorInterface;
use Shopware\Core\Checkout\Cart\LineItem\CartDataCollection;
use Shopware\Core\System\SalesChannel\SalesChannelContext;
interface QuoteClient { public function quote(array $ids): float; }
final class QuoteProcessor implements CartProcessorInterface {
    public function __construct(private QuoteClient $client) {}
    public function process(CartDataCollection $data, Cart $original, Cart $toCalculate, SalesChannelContext $context, CartBehavior $behavior): void {
        $quote = $this->client->quote($original->getLineItems()->getKeys());
        $data->set('example.quote', $quote);
    }
}

findings.behavior: The registered processor performs an external quote call on each calculation invocation, ignoring collected data. Recalculation can repeat external I/O and return inconsistent inputs during one cart flow.
findings.minimal_fix: Collect external data in a CartDataCollectorInterface implementation with a deterministic input key and has/get guard; let the processor consume collected data without I/O. Define freshness/failure behavior where data must survive calculations.
findings.verification: Repeated processing of one collected input performs no new network call; changed relevant inputs obtain a new quote.

must_avoid: Do not claim a measured latency or confirmed provider outage.
Do not mandate a new admin endpoint absent an actual operational need.

<?php
namespace Example;
use Shopware\Core\System\SalesChannel\SalesChannelContext;
use Symfony\Contracts\Cache\CacheInterface;
use Symfony\Contracts\Cache\ItemInterface;
interface PriceSource { public function forCustomer(string $product, string $customer, string $currency): int; }
final class PriceService {
    public function __construct(private CacheInterface $cache, private PriceSource $source) {}
    public function get(string $productId, SalesChannelContext $context): int {
        $customer = $context->getCustomer();
        if (!$customer) { throw new \RuntimeException('Login required'); }
        return $this->cache->get('price.' . $productId, function (ItemInterface $item) use ($productId, $context, $customer): int {
            $item->expiresAfter(120);
            return $this->source->forCustomer($productId, $customer->getId(), $context->getCurrencyId());
        });
    }
}

findings.behavior: A shared product-only key stores a value dependent on customer and currency. Another customer or currency can reuse the first result until expiry.
findings.minimal_fix: Include the effective pricing audience/customer and currency in a deterministic key, plus any proven source dependencies, or disable shared caching for these prices.
findings.verification: Request the same product in A/B/A customer and currency contexts; each receives its own source-derived amount.

must_avoid: TTL alone is not audience isolation.
Do not assert HTTP-cache or CDN leakage; only the supplied application cache is proven.

<?php
namespace Example;
use PDO;
interface ExportSink { public function publish(string $jobId, string $payload): void; }
final class ExportJob { public function __construct(public string $id) {} }
final class ExportHandler {
    public function __construct(private PDO $db, private ExportSink $sink) {}
    public function __invoke(ExportJob $message): void {
        $q = $this->db->prepare('SELECT status, payload FROM export_job WHERE id = ?');
        $q->execute([$message->id]);
        $job = $q->fetch(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);
        if (!$job || $job['status'] !== 'pending') { return; }
        $this->sink->publish($message->id, $job['payload']);
        $q = $this->db->prepare("UPDATE export_job SET status = 'done' WHERE id = ?");
        $q->execute([$message->id]);
    }
}
files.schema.sql: CREATE TABLE export_job (id VARCHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY, status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, payload TEXT NOT NULL);

findings.behavior: Both workers can read pending and publish before either updates done. The final update cannot claim the work before the side effect.
findings.minimal_fix: Use an atomic claim/lease and verify claim ownership before publish; account for crash recovery and sink deduplication or unknown outcomes.
findings.verification: Synchronize two workers after SELECT and demonstrate only the claimant publishes; test interruption after publish.

must_avoid: Do not claim a particular transport offers exactly-once delivery.
A transaction without locking/atomic claim is not itself a concurrency fix.

<?php
// Abstract contract excerpt verified against Shopware v6.7.15.1:
// https://github.com/shopware/shopware/blob/v6.7.15.1/src/Core/Framework/DataAbstractionLayer/Indexing/EntityIndexer.php
// This is source evidence, not an installed vendor package.
namespace Shopware\Core\Framework\DataAbstractionLayer\Indexing;
use Shopware\Core\Framework\DataAbstractionLayer\Event\EntityWrittenContainerEvent;
abstract class EntityIndexer {
    abstract public function getName(): string;
    abstract public function iterate(?array $offset): ?EntityIndexingMessage;
    abstract public function update(EntityWrittenContainerEvent $event): ?EntityIndexingMessage;
    abstract public function handle(EntityIndexingMessage $message): void;
    abstract public function getTotal(): int;
    abstract public function getDecorated(): EntityIndexer;
}

findings.behavior: The concrete EntityIndexer subclass omits abstract getDecorated(), so the class cannot be loaded as a concrete indexer on 6.7.15.1.
findings.minimal_fix: Implement the complete matching-version EntityIndexer contract, including getDecorated() with DecorationPatternException for a non-decorator.
findings.verification: Load the subclass against the supplied verified abstract contract, then validate real container discovery in an installed environment.

must_avoid: Do not invent additional abstract methods from another version.
The deliberately empty iteration body alone does not prove lost catalog data without requirements.

<?php
namespace Example;
use Shopware\Core\Checkout\Cart\Cart;
use Shopware\Core\Checkout\Cart\CartBehavior;
use Shopware\Core\Checkout\Cart\CartDataCollectorInterface;
use Shopware\Core\Checkout\Cart\LineItem\CartDataCollection;
use Shopware\Core\Framework\DataAbstractionLayer\EntityRepository;
use Shopware\Core\Framework\DataAbstractionLayer\Search\Criteria;
use Shopware\Core\System\SalesChannel\SalesChannelContext;
final class ProductCollector implements CartDataCollectorInterface {
    public function __construct(private EntityRepository $products) {}
    public function collect(CartDataCollection $data, Cart $original, SalesChannelContext $context, CartBehavior $behavior): void {
        $ids = [];
        foreach ($original->getLineItems() as $item) {
            if ($item->getType() === 'product' && $item->getReferencedId() !== null) { $ids[] = $item->getReferencedId(); }
        }
        $ids = array_values(array_unique($ids));
        sort($ids, SORT_STRING);
        if ($ids === []) { return; }
        $key = 'example.products.' . hash('sha256', json_encode([$ids, $context->getContext()->getVersionId(), $context->getContext()->getLanguageIdChain()], JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR));
        if ($data->has($key)) { return; }
        $data->set($key, $this->products->search(new Criteria($ids), $context->getContext())->getEntities());
    }
}

required_behavior: Recognize batched DAL reads in the collector, a deterministic input key and CartDataCollection reuse.
Distinguish per-calculation collection data from a shared external-API cache; no network client or cross-request cache is supplied.
Do not assert test execution or full integration correctness without running it.
must_avoid: Do not require a TTL or an admin invalidation route for CartDataCollection.
Do not claim a processor does database I/O when this class is a registered collector.
